paper.title: Nearly Dimension-Independent Sparse Linear Bandit over Small Action Spaces via Best Subset Selection

settings.name_in_paper: High-dimensional sparse linear stochastic contextual bandit with finite random action spaces
unmapped: each round has exactly k actions whose covariates X_{t,i} are drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution P_0 (fresh action set every round)
covariates are centered sub-Gaussian with parameter sigma_X^2 >= 1, have independent coordinates, and E[X_j^2] >= rho for every coordinate
the learner knows the covariate sub-Gaussian parameter sigma_X and the non-degeneracy constant rho (used in tuning n_0 and alpha)
settings.definition_quote: We consider finite action spaces $\{\mathcal A_t\}_{t=1}^T$ and assume that there exists some constant $k$ such that $|\mathcal A_t|=k$. We also assume that for each period $t$, the covariates $\{ X_{t,i}\}_{i \in \cA_t}$ are sampled independently from an unknown distribution $P_0$. ... (B1) Sparsity ... $|\supp(\theta^*)|=s$. (B2) $\|\theta^*\|\leq r$. (C1) The random noises are independent, centered, and sub-Gaussian with parameter $\nu^2\geq 1$.

symbols.n_0: pure-exploration length, n_0 ~ rho^-1 (nu sigma_X tau_tilde)^2 s^3 log^4(kTd/(delta lam))
symbols.alpha_1: confidence parameter alpha = sigma_X*nu*sqrt(s*tau_tilde)*log(sigma_X rho^-1 d k T/delta)
symbols.rho: lower bound on coordinate second moments of covariates

conditions: Assumptions 1-3: covariates centered sub-Gaussian(sigma_X^2>=1), independent coordinates, E[X_j^2]>=rho
noise sub-Gaussian with parameter nu^2 >= 1 (nu mapped to sigma)
tuning: n_0 ~ rho^-1 (nu sigma tau_tilde)^2 s^3 log^4(kTd/(delta lambda))
alpha = sigma nu sqrt(s tau_tilde) log(sigma rho^-1 dkT/delta)

source.label: theorem1

results.notes: Paper summarizes the dominating term as O_tilde(s sqrt(T)). Probability 1-C*delta per paper's convention. Best subset selection is NP-hard, hence compute marked exponential. lam is ridge penalty.

symbols.n_0: pure-exploration length, n_0 ~ rho^-1 (nu sigma_X tau_tilde)^2 s^3 log^4(kTd/(delta lam))
symbols.rho: lower bound on coordinate second moments of covariates

conditions: Assumptions 1-3: covariates centered sub-Gaussian(sigma_X^2>=1), independent coordinates, E[X_j^2]>=rho
tuning: n_0 ~ rho^-1 (nu sigma tau_tilde)^2 s^3 log^4(kTd/(delta lambda))

source.label: theorem2

results.notes: Paper summarizes dominant term as O_tilde(sqrt(sT)). Note n_0*beta term scales as s^3.5 polylog, independent of T up to logs.

source.label: cor:main
source.quote: We assume that $|\mathcal A_t|=k$, $X_{t,i}\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim}\mathcal N(0, I_d)$, and $\varepsilon_t\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim}\mathcal N(0,1)$, for each $1\le t\le T$. Then there exists a policy $\pi$ such that with probability at least $1-\delta$, for all $\|\theta^*\|_0\leq s$ and $\|\theta^*\|\leq r$, $R_T(\{i_t\};\theta^*) \lesssim \sqrt{sT}\cdot \mathrm{polylog}(k,d,T,r)$

results.notes: Simplified Gaussian special case of Theorem 2; polylog factors in k,d,T,r hidden. Stated as holding even if T << d (note: the s^3.5 polylog burn-in term is hidden in the paper's simplification).
